archetype.name: Game Manager (mobile backup)
archetype.definition: A quick-game, high-completion backup who keeps the offense on schedule with throws behind and just past the line, adds a few runs, and avoids interceptions, but gives back yardage by holding the ball into sacks.

report.headline: Steady three-start fill-in whose line was sunk by one bad cameo, now on IR
report.take:
Tyler Huntley is what he has been for six years: the Ravens' emergency answer when Lamar Jackson is down. He keeps the ball out of harm's way and moves the chains underneath. This season he played the role well enough. In his three starts (Weeks 5-7) he posted +0.088 EPA per dropback and a 68% completion rate, with only one interception and four touchdowns. That is clearly better than the league-average passer's -0.027. The 30-23 win in Atlanta as a 3.5-point underdog was his best day: 24 of 32, two total touchdowns and 24 PPR points.

The season line looks flatter than that because of one game. In Week 8 at Buffalo he came in for 20% of the snaps, went 2 of 4 for 0 yards, took a sack, lost a fumble and cost -7.2 EPA. That cameo is why his last-three window reads -0.019 EPA per dropback and why the whole season sits at a modest +0.022. Read the starts and the relief appearance separately. The starts are the real Huntley. Buffalo was a cold-off-the-bench mess in a 10-36 blowout.

The numbers also hide a profile that is narrower than the 69.1% completion rate suggests. His intended air yards are only 6.69, 2.25 yards short of the sticks on average, and his aggressiveness rate is low. The site's CPOE of +2.94 ranks 13th, but Next Gen's own completion model has him at -3.24, which points to the completion rate coming from easy throws. Throws behind the line (92% completions, +0.203 EPA) and 10-19 yard throws (+0.473 EPA on 22 attempts) carried the passing game. The 56 short throws in between were slightly negative. Deep, he hit one of seven. Two weaknesses run through his whole career. He turns pressure into sacks: 39.3% this year, and a poor rank every season on record. His bad-throw rate also climbed every week he started, from 9.7% to 19.4% to 23.5%.

Where it heads is mostly out of his hands. He is on injured reserve and listed as QB5. Jacoby Brissett started Week 11, and Jackson is targeting a Week 16 return from thumb surgery. Huntley's 2026 may already be over as a contributor. If he does come back, expect the Weeks 5-7 version: roughly league-average efficiency, few turnovers, too many sacks.

strengths.title: Ball security without the checkdown tax
strengths.body: His 0.9% interception rate ranks 9th of 55. In his three starts he still produced positive passing EPA every week (3.6, 3.6, 2.2). He gets there by throwing on time to defined reads rather than forcing tight windows. That fits a career with low interception counts, including none in 2025. It is the most durable part of his game.

strengths.title: Intermediate throws and screens carried it
strengths.body: His 22 throws of 10-19 air yards produced +0.473 EPA each, despite a 54.5% completion rate. Throws behind the line returned +0.203 EPA with a 92% completion rate. The screen game is scheme-built and repeatable. The intermediate number is a small sample that probably runs a bit hot, but it shows he can punish zone windows when he does push the ball.

strengths.title: Accuracy above his history's floor
strengths.body: A +2.94 CPOE ranking 13th lines up with his 2022 (+3.18) and 2024 (+3.1) seasons. This is a real trait at his chosen depths, not a fluke. Last year's +12.9 was the outlier, and this year's drop from it is mostly a return to normal.

concerns.title: Holds it into sacks, as always
concerns.body: He turns 39.3% of pressures into sacks (38th of 45), and his 9.1% sack rate ranks 41st of 55. This is not an offensive-line problem that appeared this year. His pressure-to-sack rates have been poor every season on record. The sacks are why his EPA across all dropbacks is negative while his passing EPA is positive. Nine scrambles produced zero first downs, so the extended plays aren't paying for those sacks.

concerns.title: Throw quality slipped as he played more
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate of 17.3% is 6.9 points worse than last year's. It rose with each start, finishing at 23.5% against Cincinnati. Throws over the middle were a problem: 50% completions with a -17.1 CPOE. Mark Andrews' targets cost -0.605 EPA each. Some of that is a small sample, but it suggests defenses found the windows he struggles in.

concerns.title: Availability and the depth chart
concerns.body: He is on injured reserve, did not practice before Week 9, and is listed fifth on the depth chart. Brissett took the Week 11 start. Even healthy, Huntley's path to snaps runs only until Jackson's possible Week 16 return.

trend.note: His efficiency held in Weeks 5-6 and dipped in Week 7 while his bad-throw rate climbed. The Week 8 relief cameo (-7.2 EPA) and the injury that followed ended the run.

nextGame.headline: On IR at Houston; a sack-heavy front would test him
nextGame.body:
Huntley is on injured reserve and Brissett started last week, so he is not expected to play in Houston. If he were active, the matchup would hit his main weakness. Houston's 8.9% sack rate ranks 3rd, and he already takes sacks at a bottom-tier rate. There would be openings: Houston ranks 31st in explosive pass rate allowed and 22nd in deep EPA. But his game rarely attacks deep, so he is poorly built to take advantage.

On Houston's side, edge rusher Danielle Hunter (76% of snaps) is out, which takes some heat off whoever plays quarterback for Baltimore. Rankins is questionable after an ankle injury. Baltimore is a 6.5-point underdog with a +251 moneyline, reflecting a team on its third or fourth quarterback of the year. For Huntley himself, the matchup is moot until he is activated.

keyMatchups.title: Houston's pass rush vs. his sack habit
keyMatchups.body: Houston ranks 3rd in sack rate, and Huntley converts pressure to sacks at one of the worst rates among qualifiers. Hunter's absence softens the rush, but the core problem is how long he holds the ball, and that comes with him.

keyMatchups.title: Explosive plays available, rarely taken
keyMatchups.body: Houston gives up explosive passes at the second-worst rate in the league. Huntley hit one of seven deep attempts this year and works mostly short of the sticks. The opening suits a different quarterback more than him.

keyMatchups.title: Tight ends get shut down here
keyMatchups.body: Houston has held top tight ends 3 PPR points under their usual output, 3rd-best in the league. Huntley's tight-end targets were already split: Cuevas productive, Andrews deeply negative. That leaves the ball funneling to Flowers.

nextGame.watch: Whether Baltimore activates him from IR at all, or keeps riding Brissett until Jackson's possible Week 16 return.

restOfSeason.body: The likeliest outcome is that Huntley plays little or nothing the rest of the way. He is on IR, sits fifth on the depth chart, and Jackson is aiming for Week 16. If he does start again, the three-start sample is the right baseline: a short, on-time passer with a near league-average yardage output, very few interceptions and a steady stream of sacks. The ranges below assume he starts. Expect the 10-19 yard efficiency to cool from its small-sample high. Expect the sack rate to stay where it is, since it has been his signature for years.

confidence.note: Three starts, a blowout relief cameo, and he is on IR at QB5.
